cold: Press Tab. The menu won't open.
menu: Turn on the Curb Cut Chrome extension.
Same keys. Now the menu opens.
problem: For millions of people, this is the web. Menus that only work with a mouse. Buttons with no name. Text too faint to read.
95.9 percent of the top million home pages have barriers like these.
wait: Websites take years to fix them. The people shut out can't wait that long.
title: Curb Cut fixes them now, right in your browser.
names: A screen reader used to say just, button. Now it says, previous slide.
proof: And no fix ships on a guess. Kane, an AI tester, tries the task the way a disabled person would. Without the fix, it fails. With the fix, it passes. That recording is the proof.
scale: 105 fixes are live today, and every one shows its proof.
jev: On sites we've never seen, Jev names unlabelled buttons in about a second. When it isn't sure, it stays quiet.
owner: Then the fix goes to the site owner, so one day, nobody needs us.
close: Curb Cut. Fixing the web for the people it shuts out.
